Subject: Draft: Collaboration playbook & 30-day MAP for Novanet - please review

Hi Carolyn —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, I put together a compact Mutual Action Plan focused on a 30-day evaluation-to-pilot path with clear owners, acceptance criteria, and key risks flagged. The doc is intentionally concise so your team can scan and comment quickly.

Highlights in this draft:
- Week 0: Account setup + access (dev account + sandbox data) — owner: Novanet IT
- Week 1: Integration PoC (API keys, sample flows) — owner: Novanet engineering / Redwood integration engineer
- Week 2: Performance + quality checks (latency targets, eval prompt set) — owner: Novanet product & Redwood ML eng
- Week 3: Security & compliance review (evidence for SOC2 / data handling) — owner: Novanet security + Redwood security
- Week 4: Acceptance demo + decision meeting (success criteria checklist) — owner: joint

I'd appreciate it if you could: 1) drop comments directly in the GDoc, 2) flag any scheduling constraints, and 3) confirm who from Novanet should be marked as owner for Week 2 (engineering lead vs. product).

I attached: Novanet_MAP_draft_v1.gdoc (edit link below) and a 2-slide summary you can share with stakeholders. Also including a stubbed security questionnaire for your compliance team to review.

Proposed next steps:
- Carolyn: quick review and owner assignments by Mon 4/5
- Redwood: incorporate feedback and send final MAP by Tue 4/6
- Schedule 30-min alignment call Wed 4/7 if there are unresolved items

GDoc (view/comment): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy-example-novanet-map

Thanks —

Ben —

Appreciate the clear structure. Quick notes from my side after a 15-minute skim:
- Week 0 owner: I'll own account setup with our IT contact (copying procurement for any billing/legal items)
- Week 1: We need Redwood to provide a small sample dataset and a Postman collection for the PoC — can you attach that?
- Week 2 owner should be our engineering lead (I will confirm name Mon) — please add a line for the expected latency SLOs (p50/p95) we discussed.
- Week 3: Our security team prefers evidence via a short artifact bundle rather than running through the whole questionnaire initially — can Redwood produce an evidence pack (SOC2 scope, data retention policy excerpt, and a runbook)?

One more ask: can you shorten the acceptance criteria into a 1-page checklist suitable for our leadership? I can share that with the decision committee.

On the timeline: 30 days is aggressive but plausible if we keep to the owners and have a weekly sync — I can commit to that cadence.

Thanks —
Carolyn Jackson
